title: Development of Teaching Competency in Physical Education Teacher Education Students Through Critical Pedagogy: A Mixed-Methods Analysis
text_snippet: Development of Teaching Competency in Physical Education Teacher Education Students Through Critical Pedagogy: A Mixed-Methods Analysis Purpose : This study aimed to analyze the benefits of critical pedagogy regarding the development of teaching competency (TC) of Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) students ( n = 20). title: Time for Elementary Physical Education and Estimated Energy Expenditure Based on U.S. Teacher Reporting: Implications for Strong Policy Development
text_snippet: Time for Elementary Physical Education and Estimated Energy Expenditure Based on U.S. Teacher Reporting: Implications for Strong Policy Development Purpose : We examined differences in teacher-reported weekly elementary physical education (PE) minutes by state policy type and updated previous estimates of energy expenditure (in kilocalories [kcal]) in PE. Method : Comparisons between states based on their PE time policies (no, nonspecific, noncodified, and codified) were conducted for PE minutes per week—as reported by 7,006 U.S. physical educators—and time discrepancies (teacher reported – policy-stated minutes per week). Using the same reported times, boys’ and girls’ energy expenditure were calculated overall and by state using a standard equation. Results : States with codified time policies had significantly lower time discrepancies between teacher-reported and policy-stated PE minutes per week ( p = .01). Boys and girls could expend an estimated 47,419 and 40,978 kcal, respectively, during PE across 6 years (Grades K–5). Discussion/Conclusion : Codified PE time policies with strong language (e.g., “required” and “shall”) and institutionalized accountability measures could diminish gaps between policy-recommended versus teacher-delivered PE minutes and potentiate energy expenditure.

title: “In the Line of Fire”: Critical Race Counternarratives From Black and Latine Physical Education and Teacher Education Faculty
text_snippet: “In the Line of Fire”: Critical Race Counternarratives From Black and Latine Physical Education and Teacher Education Faculty Purpose : The research highlights participants’ counternarratives as a “wake-up” call in response to dominant white discourse in higher education, analyzing the field’s historic and contemporary racialized barriers. Method : Grounded in critical race theory, the study employed visual narrative methods via interviews and photo elicitation to cultivate a collective critical race counternarrative. Results : Findings provide examples of openly racist instances and subtler reminders of “othering,” from being “the only one” to feeling a lack of belonging, tokenized within white spaces, and a sense that academic spaces are “not for me.” Discussion/Conclusion : Results evidence how Black and Latine faculty still occupy a “raced” position within physical education teacher education and endure glaring instances of racism as normalized. White physical education teacher education faculty are urged to engage in continuous inward race reflection, joining physical education teacher education Faculty of Color who have taken outright actions toward disrupting white supremacy and working for racial equity.

title: Physical Education Teachers’ Common Content Knowledge of Health-Related Fitness
text_snippet: Physical Education Teachers’ Common Content Knowledge of Health-Related Fitness Purpose : The study focused on examining in-service physical education (PE) teachers’ common content knowledge of health-related fitness. Methods : Participants were 440 in-service PE teachers (elementary PreK–5 = 202, intermediate 5–6 = 56, secondary 6–12 = 181) from eight independent school districts from various regions of the southwestern United States. The data sources included a demographic questionnaire and a 40-item health-related fitness knowledge test previously developed and validated by Santiago and Morrow. Results : In-service teachers’ mean percentage of correct scores on the health-related fitness knowledge test was 54.3% ( M = 21.7, SD = 4.6, range: 6–34). Independent t test and analyses of variance revealed that common content knowledge of health-related fitness was not a function of demographic variables. Discussion/Conclusion : Based on the results of this study, school administrators, professional organizations, and PE teacher education programs must strengthen the development of fitness content knowledge in PE.

title: Recognizing Marginality and Coping With the Challenges: A Mixed-Methods Exploration of Tasmanian Physical Educators
text_snippet: Recognizing Marginality and Coping With the Challenges: A Mixed-Methods Exploration of Tasmanian Physical Educators Purpose : Physical education (PE) is often marginalized and perceived as less academically rigorous and important than other subjects. Teachers of marginalized subjects experience many challenges, but less is known about how they cope and persist in the profession. The purpose of this study was to utilize Appraisal Theory and coping literature to ascertain Tasmanian PE teacher challenges and coping mechanisms. Methods : A mixed methods approach was used. Survey data ( N = 88) helped identify top-ranked sources of perceived marginality followed by individual interviews ( n = 19) identifying the top coping mechanisms. Results : Findings indicated that key challenges included a lack of time to cover required content and fulfill professional duties, difficulties with national curriculum planning and assessment, and others’ perceptions of the value of PE. Conclusion : Teacher appraisals of their status help inform how they feel and cope. Teachers use a variety of functional and dysfunctional coping strategies, and more training is needed.

title: Wash in, But: The Influence of Contextual Factors on Preservice Teachers’ Use of the Game Sense Approach During Field Experiences
text_snippet: Wash in, But: The Influence of Contextual Factors on Preservice Teachers’ Use of the Game Sense Approach During Field Experiences Purpose : Pedagogies and teaching approaches learned at universities can be “washed out” of physical education teachers when they begin working in schools. However, less research has examined whether they have been adequately “washed in” to preservice teachers at universities. This study utilized occupational socialization theory to investigate whether the game sense approach had been adequately washed into Australian preservice teachers. Methods : A mixed methods approach was used. Survey data ( N = 52) helped identify whether wash-in had occurred, before individual interviews ( n = 20) identified the influence of acculturation, professional socialization, and contextual factors on field experiences. Results : Findings indicated that wash-in had occurred to some extent and that preservice teachers intended to use the approach. However, use was limited by contextual factors such as content, student behavior, and team teaching. Conclusion : Organizational socialization is often to blame for washout. However, more information should be collected on professional socialization.

text_snippet: Compete With a Purpose, Bring Home a Ring: Impact of Sport Education on Incarcerated Young Adults Health-Related Fitness Markers Purpose : Despite knowledge promoting physical activity as a key factor in maintaining overall well-being, there are notable discrepancies in the levels of physical activity among incarcerated young adults. title: “It’s Gonna Take Time”: Enacting Culturally Relevant Physical Education in Urban Schools
text_snippet: “It’s Gonna Take Time”: Enacting Culturally Relevant Physical Education in Urban Schools Guided by culturally relevant physical education, the purpose of this single case study was to examine how one PE teacher in a culturally and ethnically diverse urban school implemented strategies that reflected cultural knowledge. To accomplish this, one participant completed five semi-structured interviews, five reflection journal prompts, and eight voice memos 12 weeks. Preexisting data included a semi-structured interview with John completed in May 2021 and documents, such as lesson plans, reflections, and assignments from John’s teacher preparation program. Three themes were constructed: (1) Teaching beyond the script: Personalizing curriculum to reflect student lives; (2) More than a teacher: Investing in schoolwide change; and (3) Pedagogical and structural adjustments to the class. This research is significant because it highlights strategies physical education teacher education programs and in-service teachers may utilize to bridge cultural distance between their own backgrounds and lived experiences, and those of their culturally and ethnically diverse students.

title: Investigating the Influence of Occupational Socialization on the Career Paths of Physical Educators
text_snippet: Investigating the Influence of Occupational Socialization on the Career Paths of Physical Educators Purpose : This qualitative study examined how occupational socialization shaped the long-term career trajectories of physical education (PE) teachers. Method : Guided by Fessler and Christensen’s Career Cycle Model and an interpretive paradigm, the study explored the lived experiences of 10 American PE teachers who graduated from the same teacher education program. Participants were categorized as Remainers—those who stayed in PE teaching or related roles—and Exiters—those who left the profession. Results : Most were Remainers who advanced through career stages with support from mentorship, leadership roles, and a strong professional identity. Exiters faced burnout, marginalization, or systemic barriers that contributed to attrition. Discussion/Conclusion : Across both groups, personal dispositions, early sport experiences, societal expectations, and school organizational culture were influential. The findings also reflect the push, pull, and keep factor framework, indicating that PE teacher retention is shaped by broader system dynamics. The study calls for systemic supports to foster sustainable, fulfilling careers.

title: What Makes Preservice Teachers Learning Effective? Unveiling Characteristics of Practice-Based Teacher Education
text_snippet: What Makes Preservice Teachers Learning Effective? Unveiling Characteristics of Practice-Based Teacher Education Purpose : The authors aimed to explore meaningful characteristics of practice-based teacher education that facilitate physical education preservice teachers’ (PTs’) learning about a pedagogical model called Hanaro Teaching. Method : A qualitative case study design was adopted to focus primarily on a group of PTs in the Eastern United States. Eight PTs were selected as participants. Throughout one semester, PTs learned the model through a series of learning activities. Data were gathered through individual interviews, observation/field notes, and participants’ written materials. Findings : Five themes were identified during the analysis process: (a) confusion to confidence through repetition across formats; (b) I trust their feedback; (c) the more examples, the better understanding; (d) conference presentation as reflection-on-action; and (e) critical friends through cohort camaraderie. Discussion and Conclusion : The findings indicated that the characteristics of deliberate practice and reflection helped PTs learn the pedagogical model. This demonstrates the usefulness of the practice-based teacher education.

title: The Impact of Content Knowledge on Micro- and Macroadaptive Teaching and Children’s Learning in Primary Physical Education
text_snippet: The Impact of Content Knowledge on Micro- and Macroadaptive Teaching and Children’s Learning in Primary Physical Education Purpose : This study explored how content knowledge (CK) affects both micro- and macroadaptive teaching, with a focus on microadaptivity, in fourth-grade physical education classes. Methods : In a pre–post design, two female preservice physical education teachers (PSTs) participated in a workshop to enhance their CK for teaching the squat vault (gymnastics) and “moving to get open” (basketball). Microadaptive teaching was assessed through PST responses, task instructions, and student performance; macroadaptivity was analyzed via lesson plans. Results : After the workshop, PSTs identified errors more accurately. The proportion of task instructions addressing student errors increased, and student performance improved in both skills. Lesson plans reflected higher quality content development. Conclusion : CK played a vital role in improving both micro- and macroadaptive teaching. In particular, CK helped PSTs respond more effectively to student needs during instruction.

title: Middle School Students’ Perceptions of Movement Integration

title: An Ecological Perspective on Physical Education Teacher Education: Lessons Learned From Novice Teachers’ Perceptions and Experiences
text_snippet: An Ecological Perspective on Physical Education Teacher Education: Lessons Learned From Novice Teachers’ Perceptions and Experiences This study aimed to explore the ecology of teacher preparation, specifically focusing on preservice teachers’ development and teaching practices throughout their experience in a physical education teacher education (PETE) program. Using a qualitative case study design, participants included four novice physical education teachers. Data were collected through semistructured interviews, critical incident timelines, structured observations, and artifacts. Results are presented according to the five systems of Bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory, including: PETE coursework as a foundation, the importance of involvement outside of PETE, the crucial links between PETE and community, the negligible influence of negative factors, and the dynamic process of teacher education. The findings of the study demonstrate how various ecological systems within a PETE program contribute to preservice teachers’ development. The study suggests that PETE programs could enhance their curriculum by fostering interactions across different ecological systems to optimize preservice teachers’ learning and professional readiness.

title: Emotional Labor of Physical Education Teachers: Portrait Vignettes on Genuine Expression in French Compensatory Education
text_snippet: Emotional Labor of Physical Education Teachers: Portrait Vignettes on Genuine Expression in French Compensatory Education Purpose : This aim of this study was to investigate physical education teachers’ genuine expression of positive and negative emotions during critical incidents in French compensatory education. Method : Adopting a situational approach to emotional labor, we conducted interviews with 22 teachers in which they retold the five critical incidents they had described in writing during the school year. Results : According to the systematic analysis conducted, teachers genuinely expressed their emotions 78/110 times (70.9%), combining genuine expression with active strategies of emotional labor in certain situations. Statistical analysis revealed that the teachers tended to adopt the strategy of genuine expression only when they felt positive emotions and to combine it with active strategies of emotional labor when they felt negative ones. Four portrait vignettes are presented to illustrate the complex enacted forms of genuine expression in critical classroom situations. Discussion/Conclusion : These results provide a new understanding of the complexity of genuine expression in physical education teaching in the field of compensatory education.

title: Understanding the Use of Motor Competence Assessments in Australian Elementary Physical Education: A Qualitative Study
text_snippet: Understanding the Use of Motor Competence Assessments in Australian Elementary Physical Education: A Qualitative Study Purpose : Developing motor competence (MC) is a key objective of elementary health and physical education (HPE) curricula in Australia, which includes explicit assessment. However, the use of valid, reliable, and feasible MC assessments by elementary HPE teachers is largely unknown. This study aims to: (i) understand the use of evidence-based MC assessments by Victorian HPE teachers, and (ii) explore barriers and facilitators from teacher and stakeholder perspectives. Method : Semistructured online interviews were conducted with 16 participants, including eight Victorian HPE teachers and eight Australian education stakeholders. The Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior model framed the interview questions and thematic data analysis. Results : Teachers rarely used evidence-based assessment tools and often developed their own. Barriers included insufficient resources, support, and training. Stakeholders noted inadequate teacher preparation for MC assessment. Facilitators included technology and support materials/resources. Discussion / Conclusion : Enhancing teacher education and access to evidence-based MC assessments may improve MC teaching quality and student MC.

title: Following Preservice Physical Education Teachers’ Development and Construction of Knowledge for Marginality and Mattering Beliefs Across Their Physical Education Teacher Education Program
text_snippet: Following Preservice Physical Education Teachers’ Development and Construction of Knowledge for Marginality and Mattering Beliefs Across Their Physical Education Teacher Education Program Purpose: Despite the role of physical education teacher education (PETE) programs in preparing physical education (PE) teachers, there seems to be a gap in sociopolitical training. The purpose of this study was to explore preservice teachers (PSTs) awareness and construction of their knowledge of marginality and mattering of PE across their PETE program. Methods: PSTs ( N = 9) completed multiple semistructured interviews and journaling sessions across four semesters of PETE. A qualitative interpretative design was used to analyze data. Results: Findings revealed PSTs entered the program with no sociopolitical knowledge about teaching PE. Three themes were found: (a) acculturation experiences do not afford knowledge of marginality or mattering of PE, (b) field experiences provided the greatest source of knowledge of marginality and mattering, and (c) PE teacher quality is the strongest predictor of a school’s value of PE. Conclusion: PSTs need systematic training on the realities of the profession, and PETE programs must provide it.

title: The Impact of Physical Activity on Academic Performance of Adolescents From a Neurocognitive Perspective: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: The Impact of Physical Activity on Academic Performance of Adolescents From a Neurocognitive Perspective: A Systematic Review Learning is one of the most critical developmental tasks during adolescence. Drawing on evidence from neurocognitive science, this study examines the effects of physical activity on academic performance. The review found that physical activity improves healthy fitness, executive function, and learning behaviors in adolescents, which in turn improves academic performance. In terms of mechanisms, physical activity promotes microadaptive changes in neurofactors, such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor, insulin-like growth factor 1, and vascular endothelial growth factor and their receptors, and macroregulates the volume of brain structures such as white and gray matter, as well as brain activation patterns. Therefore, physical education should incorporate the cross-cutting benefits of cognitive neuroscience to promote the physical health and brain development of adolescents, so that “home, school, and society” can re-conceptualize the multifaceted value of physical education for the overall development of students.

title: Can Feedback Promote Motor Skill Acquisition in Physical Education? An Updated Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis
text_snippet: Can Feedback Promote Motor Skill Acquisition in Physical Education? An Updated Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis Purpose : This study aims to clarify the effectiveness of feedback in promoting motor skill acquisition among students in physical education. Method : A comprehensive search of Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOHost databases was conducted through August 2024. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and data analysis was performed with Review Manager 5.4 and Trial Sequential Analysis software. Results : The meta-analysis of 20 studies ( N = 1,162) found that feedback significantly improved motor skill acquisition in physical education ( Z = 5.63; p Z = 3.68; p Z = 5.14; p Z curve crossed only the traditional boundary. Conclusion : Although feedback enhances motor skill learning in physical education, the evidence is not yet conclusive, necessitating further research to substantiate these findings.

title: Teachers’ Pedagogical Decisions to Promote Group Cohesion and Psychological Needs: Exploring Cooperative Learning, Team Building, and Direct Instruction
text_snippet: Teachers’ Pedagogical Decisions to Promote Group Cohesion and Psychological Needs: Exploring Cooperative Learning, Team Building, and Direct Instruction Purpose : This study aimed to assess in which order to implement cooperative learning (CL), team building (TB), and direct instruction (DI) to promote class cohesion and students’ basic psychological needs. Method : A school-based quasiexperimental design was used with 690 participants, including three experimental conditions and pre- and postintervention measures. A longitudinal, counterbalanced design controlled the sequence of three learning units: Group 1 (CL–TB–DI), Group 2 (TB–DI–CL), and Group 3 (DI–CL–TB). Results : CL and TB produced significant increases in the students’ task and social cohesion and all basic psychological needs, while DI only increased task cohesion and competence (although both limited). Long-term results showed that only CL produced significant increases in all variables. Conclusion : Sequencing pedagogies in physical education is key. CL is the most effective for fostering cohesion and basic psychological needs, even when combined with DI, and should be implemented using frameworks like the CL cycle.

title: Teachers’ Perspectives of Social and Emotional Learning in Elementary Physical Education
text_snippet: Teachers’ Perspectives of Social and Emotional Learning in Elementary Physical Education This study aimed to investigate elementary physical education (PE) teachers’ personal and professional beliefs about social and emotional learning (SEL) and teaching SEL in the United States. The main research questions were: (1) What are elementary PE teachers’ interpretations of SEL as an educational concept within their own teaching contexts? and (2) What pedagogical approach do elementary PE teachers think is important to teach SEL within their own teaching contexts? Adopting a qualitative case study design, 22 elementary PE teachers were recruited across the United States. Semistructured interviews with an interview guide were implemented on a video-conferencing system called “Zoom.” Inductive qualitative analysis was conducted with open coding and axial coding. Five themes were generated from the data analysis: Teaching empathy has to be intentional, Recognizing and managing emotions, Creative teachable moments, Play is underrated, and It’s all about the context. We claim more empirical research should be conducted to gain a more comprehensive understanding of SEL implementation in elementary PE classes across a broad range of sociocultural contexts.

title: Development of a Competency Model for Physical Education Teachers in Inclusive Physical Education Classes: Focusing on Environments of South Korea
text_snippet: Development of a Competency Model for Physical Education Teachers in Inclusive Physical Education Classes: Focusing on Environments of South Korea Purpose : This study aimed to conduct a competency model to identify the competencies required for physical education (PE) teachers to implement inclusive PE classes (IPEC), including students with disabilities, in general PE classes in South Korea, where no specialized adapted PE teachers exist. Method : This study employed a two-round Delphi process, leveraging the expertise of the panel members ( N = 20) with a record of educational and/or academic involvement in IPEC competencies. Results : The Delphi panel evaluated the literature analysis’s initial list of 22 competencies. Fourteen competencies were identified as IPEC competencies through expert consensus. The panel then meticulously clustered these 14 competencies into four dimensions based on their semantic relationships, including IPEC student understanding competency, IPEC practice competency, IPEC communication competency, and IPEC literacy competency. Conclusions : Based on the above research results, the implications for improving PE teachers’ IPEC competency and competency development research were discussed.

title: Assessing Physical Literacy in Health and Physical Education Through Biographical Mapping
text_snippet: Assessing Physical Literacy in Health and Physical Education Through Biographical Mapping Background : Assessment plays an integral role in shaping how physical literacy (PL) is understood and enacted within Health and Physical Education (H/PE). Traditional assessments that are too linear, narrow, or focused on fixed ends can limit students’ exploration of PL. Purpose : This paper proposes a biographical mapping approach for PL (BMAP-PL), offering a conceptual and methodological approach for assessing PL that extends beyond particular physical movements and skill competencies. Approach : BMAP-PL in H/PE involves a five-step process, including mapping significant movement-related events, evaluating PL over time, and integrating reflective goal setting and assessment. This process conceptualizes PL as a dynamic, nonlinear, and individualized journey with no fixed end state. Significance : Through capturing the biographical situatedness of a student’s PL journey, BMAP-PL highlights how individualized experiences, coupled with knowledge and skill acquisition, can contribute to the ongoing development of PL, offering a meaningful and flexible assessment approach for PL in H/PE.

title: Teaching Personal and Social Responsibility in the Spanish School System: From Physical Education Toward Other Content Areas
text_snippet: Teaching Personal and Social Responsibility in the Spanish School System: From Physical Education Toward Other Content Areas Purpose : The purpose of the present study was to examine the perceptions of teachers and students regarding a teaching personal and social responsibility (TPSR)-based intervention implemented in two Spanish schools. Methods : The study included 15 teachers from different curricular areas (e.g., physical education, mathematics, and sciences) and 102 students who participated in a 7-month TPSR-based intervention. Results : Findings emphasized the importance of contextualizing TPSR to the sociocultural context per various factors, such as the pedagogical approach used, the school culture, and the curricula. Moreover, neoliberal values influenced the extent to which TPSR could become a transformative experience for teachers and youth. Moving forward, the integration of TPSR through a whole-school approach can be seen as a form of educational activism, aiming not only to focus personal and social development but also to inspire young people to become agents of change in their communities. Conclusions : TPSR in physical education can be positioned as a first step toward creating more consistent developmental objectives within the school environment.

title: From the Coach’s Perspective: Making Interscholastic Sports Inclusive for Students With and Without Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
text_snippet: From the Coach’s Perspective: Making Interscholastic Sports Inclusive for Students With and Without Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities Competing in interscholastic sports is a valuable and normative experience for high school student athletes, providing a range of benefits that enhance well-being. Yet the opportunities for youth with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) to play high school sports, although growing in recent years, remain mostly limited to the intramural level. This study focuses on the coaches of an interscholastic high school sports program offered to students with and without IDD who competed on the same team. Based on 29 interviews with 18 Unified Track-and-Field coaches from eight different teams, as part of a larger impact evaluation study of Unified Interscholastic Sports, this study shows how coaches created and facilitated the competitive environment that is vital to interscholastic sports while being inclusive of student athletes with and without IDD. Furthermore, the inclusion of youth with IDD in interscholastic sports positively contributed to the school culture and visibility in the community.

title: Improving Water Safety and Long-term Engagement in Aquatic Physical Activity: The Aquatic Literacy Framework
text_snippet: Improving Water Safety and Long-term Engagement in Aquatic Physical Activity: The Aquatic Literacy Framework Young people worldwide are affected by two main health-related issues: physical inactivity and drowning accidents. Encouraging participation in aquatic physical activities in a safe way could address this dual concern. Aligning theoretical frameworks of physical literacy and water competencies could empower young people with key skills to engage safely and sustainably in aquatic environments. The aim of this theoretical paper is to provide a philosophical, ontological, and epistemological rationale for merging these two frameworks into a new concept: aquatic literacy. The multidimensional concept is presented and describes the intertwined physical, psychosocial, and cognitive domains, which provide a means to empower young people to safely enjoy aquatic opportunities and achieve individual health benefits. This new concept needs supportive empirical data, such as the level of individuals in each domain of aquatic literacy, to be a strong framework for guiding aquatic educators and stakeholders to better engage and protect people worldwide.

title: Technology Use in Physical Education: Insights From New York State Teachers
text_snippet: Technology Use in Physical Education: Insights From New York State Teachers Purpose : This study investigated technology use among physical education teachers in New York State, focusing on the types of technology employed and the influence of demographic factors on usage. Methods : A cross-sectional design was used, with data collected via an online questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics and multiple regression. Results : Technologies ranged from basic tools like stopwatches to advanced options such as augmented reality, though the latter were less frequently used. Regression analysis indicated that demographic factors explained 25.9% of the variance in technology usage, R 2 = .259, F (14, 246) = 6.14, p p = .006), school size (β = 1.86, p p = .003). Conclusions : Addressing key predictors, such as professional development, and resource availability may bridge gaps and promote broader, more effective technology integration in physical education.

title: Service-Learning in Secondary School Physical Education Teacher Education in Taiwan: A Study on Approaches to Reflection
text_snippet: Service-Learning in Secondary School Physical Education Teacher Education in Taiwan: A Study on Approaches to Reflection Purpose : This study investigated the positive, neutral, and negative learning outcomes associated with service-learning among secondary school physical education preservice teachers in rural areas of Taiwan. Method : This study analyzed the reflections and questionnaire responses of 38 preservice teachers (26 males and 12 females) enrolled in a secondary physical education teacher education program, who participated in rural service-learning at a sport university in northern Taiwan. The information was examined using thematic analysis and interpretative phenomenological analysis. Results : The results were categorized into five themes, each focusing on different aspects of preservice teachers’ experiences in service-learning. These categories not only offered an overview of their growth and development but also shed light on the disparities and challenges within rural areas. Discussion : Service-learning enhanced the professional growth of physical education preservice teachers in Taiwan, fostering adaptability, reflection, and a commitment to addressing challenges in rural areas.

title: Physical Education Preservice Teachers’ Perspectives on Practice-Based Teacher Education Pedagogies: Teaching Rehearsals and Repeated Teaching
text_snippet: Physical Education Preservice Teachers’ Perspectives on Practice-Based Teacher Education Pedagogies: Teaching Rehearsals and Repeated Teaching Purpose : The purpose of this study was to explore preservice teachers’ perspectives on two practice-based teacher education pedagogies, teaching rehearsals and repeated teaching, in eight physical education teacher education programs. Method : We employed a multiple case study design. Thirty-eight preservice teachers (four to six per program) participated in the study (female, n = 20; male, n = 18; sophomore, n = 7; junior, n = 12; senior, and n = 19). A semistructured interview was conducted to collect data. The data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis, followed by magnitude coding. Results : Five themes were identified from the data: (a) improved practices in classroom management, (b) improved effectiveness in providing instructions, (c) enhanced content knowledge, (d) learning from peers, and (e) perspectives toward teaching rehearsals and repeated teaching. Discussion/Conclusion : The findings provide evidence of the acceptability of two practice-based teacher education pedagogies as teacher education practices by preservice teachers.

title: The Implementation of the Digital Physical Literacy for Children Questionnaire in Primary Schools: A Mixed-Methods Study
text_snippet: The Implementation of the Digital Physical Literacy for Children Questionnaire in Primary Schools: A Mixed-Methods Study Purpose : To assess the implementation of the digital version of the Physical Literacy in Children Questionnaire (PL-C Quest) in a primary school environment. Methods : A mixed-methods study with teachers ( n = 13) and students ( n = 20) about their respective reflections on administering and completing the PL-C Quest. Results : The PL-C Quest was perceived as acceptable, appropriate, and feasible. All teachers felt the PL-C Quest was easy for them, and, their students to use. Students enjoyed completing the PL-C Quest, they understood the questionnaire, and found it easy to use; teachers described the ease of administration of the PL-C Quest and their interest in the data provided. Some teachers reported concerns about the usefulness of the PL-C Quest results, highlighting that greater school-wide focus on physical literacy (including professional learning opportunities) would be required. Conclusions : The findings from this study highlight critical considerations for integrating physical literacy assessment tools into school practice.

title: Life Skills Development and Transfer of Student-Athletes in Competitive Sport: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Teaching
text_snippet: Life Skills Development and Transfer of Student-Athletes in Competitive Sport: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Teaching Purpose : In recent years, there has been increasing interest in studying coaches’ roles in promoting positive youth development through sports. Researchers suggest that coaches’ strategies, whether implicit or explicit, can influence athletes’ life skills development and transfer. However, these assumptions lacked statistical validation. Hence, this study aimed to explore the structural relationship between perceived implicit and explicit teaching and athletes’ life skills development and transfer. Method : This study surveyed data from 332 student-athletes (259 males, 73 females, average age = 18.2 years) in South Korea, utilizing structural equation modeling for analysis. Results : Findings revealed that while implicit teaching influenced life skills development, explicit teaching impacted both development and transfer. Additionally, life skills development was found to influence transfer. Discussion/Conclusion : Coaches need to consciously plan and implement life skills teaching to enhance student-athletes’ development and transfer.

title: Preservice Physical Education Teachers’ Experiences With Constraint-Led Approach: A RE-AIM Framework Evaluation
text_snippet: Preservice Physical Education Teachers’ Experiences With Constraint-Led Approach: A RE-AIM Framework Evaluation Purpose : This study investigated the experiences of 49 preservice physical education (PE) teachers as they developed and implemented PE lesson plans in a simulated classroom, guided by the constraints-led approach during ball game lessons. The aim was to explore the practical application of Newell’s constraints model within a teacher education context. Method : A single case study design was employed. Qualitative data were collected primarily from preservice PE teachers’ reflection journals, structured using the RE-AIM framework, and thematic analysis was employed to analyze the data. Results : Three main themes and 11 subthemes emerged: (a) reshaping pedagogical practices, (b) challenges in applying Newell’s constraints model, and (c) enhancement and application in teacher education programs. Discussion/Conclusion : The study results highlight the importance of understanding the subtle dynamics between constraints and instructional strategies. The findings stress the vital role of teachers in pinpointing and integrating key elements of sports performance. Through deepening our understanding of the constraints-led approach, this study suggests potential improvements in PE teaching

title: The Effect of Blended Teaching Personal and Social Responsibility on College Students’ Personal and Social Responsibilities and Prosocial Behaviors With Self-Efficacy as a Mediator
text_snippet: The Effect of Blended Teaching Personal and Social Responsibility on College Students’ Personal and Social Responsibilities and Prosocial Behaviors With Self-Efficacy as a Mediator Objective : To investigate the effects of a 16-week Blended Teaching Personal and Social Responsibility (BTPSR) intervention, applied once weekly for 90 min in rhythmic gymnastics instruction, on college students’ personal and social responsibility, prosocial behavior, and the mediating role of self-efficacy. Methods : A total of 66 first-year female college students from two classes participated in the experiment, aged 17–20 ( M = 18.39; SD = 0.653). The two classes were randomly selected and assigned as the experimental group and the control group. A 16-week teaching intervention was conducted (90 min per session), with the experimental group using BTPSR and the control group using traditional teaching methods. Results : The experimental group exhibited significant improvement in personal and social responsibility ( p p SE = 1.96, 95% confidence interval [0.10, 7.33]). Conclusion : BTPSR integration in rhythmic gymnastics significantly improved students’ personal and social responsibility and prosocial behavior, with self-efficacy mediating this enhancement. This teaching model is promising for developing students’ social competencies.

title: An In-Depth Analysis of Physical Education in Fiji’s Western Division Secondary Schools: Understanding Stakeholder Voices for Curriculum Reform
text_snippet: An In-Depth Analysis of Physical Education in Fiji’s Western Division Secondary Schools: Understanding Stakeholder Voices for Curriculum Reform Purpose : This exploratory study assesses the current status of physical education within Fiji’s secondary schools in the Western Division, focusing on the perspectives of diverse stakeholders toward curriculum reform. Method : This study employed a qualitative approach, gathering data through in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions with key stakeholders, including students, Physical Education, Music, and Art and Craft teachers, principals, parents, and Ministry of Education officials. Results : Data were analyzed with an inductive thematic analysis technique described by Braun and Clarke. Data revealed seven themes: time allocation, curriculum refinement, innovative teaching and assessment, social recognition, diverse participation, partnership, and student motivation. Conclusion : Collaborative efforts between educational institutions, government bodies, and sports organizations are required to elevate physical education’s status and have an impact on student well-being and academic success in Fiji.

title: First-Year Physical Education Teachers’ Major Sources of Efficacy: Transition From Preservice to In-Service Teaching
text_snippet: First-Year Physical Education Teachers’ Major Sources of Efficacy: Transition From Preservice to In-Service Teaching Purpose : Understanding early career physical education (PE) teachers’ experiences and how they influence teaching efficacy is essential for retention amidst reports of teacher attrition and burnout. The purpose of this study was to explore the major sources of efficacy for first-year U.S. PE teachers, which included sources from their preservice to in-service teaching experiences. Method s: As part of a larger study, the study includes individual interviews of first-year PE teachers ( N = 14) across 11 different U.S. states. Analysis was grounded in Self-Efficacy Theory using both inductive and deductive techniques. Results : Student teaching, observing cooperating teachers, principals, current students, and content knowledge were the reported factors that aligned with their sources of teaching efficacy. Conclusion : The sources of efficacy identified in this study provide insight on how early career teachers develop efficacy, which can be leveraged by both PE teacher education programs and K–12 schools to support retention and growth.

title: Feasibility of Virtual Fundamental Motor Skill Assessment Using the Test of Gross Motor Development-3
text_snippet: Feasibility of Virtual Fundamental Motor Skill Assessment Using the Test of Gross Motor Development-3 The Test of Gross Motor Development-3 is the most widely used test to assess fundamental motor skills, yet its feasibility in virtual assessments remains underexplored. The purpose of this study was twofold: (a) to examine the feasibility of conducting virtual TGMD-3 assessments by evaluating participant adherence, technological factors, environmental factors, and procedural considerations; and (b) to explore therelationship between in-person and virtual assessment scores. title: “I Need to Focus on my Family”: The Role of Family and Community for Latino Boys in an After-School Physical Activity Program
text_snippet: “I Need to Focus on my Family”: The Role of Family and Community for Latino Boys in an After-School Physical Activity Program Purpose : This yearlong qualitative case study sought to understand the lived experiences and the role of family and community among Latino boys in an after-school physical activity program. Method : Four preservice teachers facilitated the REACH after-school program and contributed weekly to a “coaches journal.” To understand the lived experience of the participants, 23 boys participated and contributed weekly journal entries. Ten boys were interviewed at the end of the program. Data were independently coded using constant comparison. Results : The results of this study are presented through two themes: (1) family and community influences and (2) role modeling. Discussion : The after-school program provided a safe space that helped discussion and deconstruction of different barriers to physical activity. Family dynamics and adult role models played a role in the boys’ engagement in physical activity and pushed them to give back to their community.

title: Physical Education Teachers’ Acceptance and Use of a Fitness-Based Software
text_snippet: Physical Education Teachers’ Acceptance and Use of a Fitness-Based Software Purpose : The purpose of this study was to explore secondary physical educators’ acceptance and use of PLT4M (“Plat-form”), a software for fitness-based curricula. Method : Cross-sectional mixed methods included a survey instrument guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) completed by secondary physical education teachers using PLT4M. Future studies including larger sample sizes and the UTAUT-2 instrument are needed to increase validity and reliability of physical education teachers’ acceptance and use of technologies. Qualitative research methods can provide insight into how teachers use specific technologies.

title: Examining the Differences in Physical Educators’ Self-Efficacy to Teach Students With Disabilities Across Instructional Placements
text_snippet: Examining the Differences in Physical Educators’ Self-Efficacy to Teach Students With Disabilities Across Instructional Placements Purpose : This study examined the differences in physical educators’ self-efficacy to teach students with disabilities across integrated and self-contained classes and the association between efficacy-relevant information on their beliefs in their capabilities to teach across each placement. Method : Physical education (PE) teachers ( n = 170) completed the Self-Efficacy to Teach Students with Disabilities Across Instructional Placements for Physical Education scale and a demographic questionnaire. Differences in self-efficacy between placements were tested using analyses of covariance, and associations between self-efficacy variables were explored via structural equation modeling. Results : No significant differences in PE teachers’ self-efficacy were found among teachers with experience teaching students with disabilities in only an integrated placement compared with a self-contained placement. title: Learning in Physical Education: A Transfer of Learning Theory Perspective
text_snippet: Learning in Physical Education: A Transfer of Learning Theory Perspective The goal of education is to develop students’ capacity to transfer knowledge and skills learned in classrooms to real life. The theory of transfer articulates near transfer (transfer between similar settings) as the foundation for far transfer (between different settings). Purpose : Based on the transfer theory, the purpose of the study was to determine the near transfer in learning caloric-balanced living concepts in high school physical education. Method : High school students ( n = 980) participated in the curriculum intervention. They learned knowledge in Unit 1 and applied the concepts in Unit 2. A pre- and postintervention design revealed the extent of knowledge near transfer from Unit 1 to Unit 2. Result : A regression analysis revealed a sizeable transfer with B = 0.32 ( p R 2 = .095; β = 0.32). Conclusion : The finding indicates a strong possibility of knowledge transfer between learning concepts and applying them in physical education.

title: Exploring Transgender and Nonbinary People’s Experiences of Cisnormative Physical Education at Secondary School
text_snippet: Exploring Transgender and Nonbinary People’s Experiences of Cisnormative Physical Education at Secondary School Purpose : There is emerging evidence that physical education (PE) can be a negative experience for transgender and nonbinary people; however, it is unclear whether this impacts levels of physical activity in adulthood. Method : Forty-two transgender and nonbinary participants completed an online survey about their experience of PE at secondary school and current levels of physical activity. Results : Most participants had negative experiences of PE. Changing rooms were a particular challenge but views differed as to the preferred solution. Factors relating to enjoyment, included participant’s feelings of competence, safety, and physical comfort. Physical comfort was significantly correlated with current levels of physical activity. Conclusions : We conclude that cisnormative sex-separated model of PE, based on binary gender organization, negatively impacts trans and nonbinary students. In addition to rethinking this model and creating an inclusive environment, it is important that school policy is adapted to support individual trans and nonbinary students.

title: Game Tactical Learning for Primary School Students With a Digital Video Analysis Tool
text_snippet: Game Tactical Learning for Primary School Students With a Digital Video Analysis Tool Purpose : This study investigated the impact of using a digital analysis tool on the tactical skills of primary school students in recognizing cover shadows and finding possible passing routes. Methods : Ninety-two students participated, with the experimental group analyzing game scenes by drawing cover shadows and passing routes using a digital tool, while the control group analyzed without digital support. Tactical skills were assessed using a coding manual adapted from the Game Performance Assessment Instrument, focusing on on- and off-ball behaviors. Results : Significant improvements were found in the experimental group for “Positioning” ( p = .016) and “Correct Ball Demand” ( p = .031), indicating better positioning to pass and more correct verbal/gestural ball demands. Conclusion : Working with a digital tool improved the students’ tactical skills. The behaviors of “Positioning” and “Correct ball demand” benefited the most, as these rely less on technical and coordinative skills compared with other tactical behaviors.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Teacher Perceptions of Physical Literacy Informed Physical Education: The Barriers and Potential Solutions
text_snippet: Teacher Perceptions of Physical Literacy Informed Physical Education: The Barriers and Potential Solutions Purpose : Physical literacy is becoming a key framework for promoting physical activity across sectors globally, particularly in physical education. This research explores how this emerging concept can be operationalized through professional development (PD) and examines teacher perceptions of barriers and solutions to embedding physical literacy in practice. Method : A 12-week PD participatory action research intervention was conducted in three U.K. schools (one primary and two secondary) with primary generalist teachers ( n = 3) and secondary physical education specialists ( n = 11). Semistructured interviews captured teacher perceptions before, after, and 3 months postintervention. Thematic analysis organized data on barriers and solutions. Results : Teachers identified barriers in four areas: leadership and governance, management and institutional, individual, and philosophy and values. Solutions focused on raising physical education’s status and improving PD opportunities. Discussion/Conclusion : The research highlights the influence of school cultures in developing physical literacy. Effective PD must consider these as well as real-life challenges to achieve lasting impact.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Toward an Understanding of the Relationship Between Professional Learning Community Engagement and Collective Teacher Efficacy Among Physical Education Teachers
text_snippet: Toward an Understanding of the Relationship Between Professional Learning Community Engagement and Collective Teacher Efficacy Among Physical Education Teachers Purpose : Professional learning communities (PLCs) serve as a framework for fostering teacher collaboration and problem-solving in schools. Collective teacher efficacy (CTE) is critical to understanding PLCs. This study explored how physical education teachers engage in PLCs and examined the relationship between their PLC engagement and CTE. Methods : This study utilized a mixed-method, explanatory sequential design where quantitative survey data collection was followed by qualitative interviews. Results : Quantitative data analysis suggests that physical educators engage moderately with PLCs and that overall engagement is highly correlated with CTE. Qualitative analysis was organized into three themes: (a) School and Team Culture as a Foundational Contributing Factor to Engagement, (b) Collective Actions as Indicators of Engaging PLC Cultures, and (c) The Intersection of Collective Efficacy and PLCs. Discussion/Conclusion : Implications include the consideration of PLC contextual influences on CTE and the growing necessity for collective action in physical education.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Influence of Institution Type on Faculty Members’ Philosophy of Physical Education Teacher Education
text_snippet: Influence of Institution Type on Faculty Members’ Philosophy of Physical Education Teacher Education Purpose : This study’s purpose was to investigate the influence of institution type on faculty members’ philosophy and implementation of physical education teacher education. Method : Participants were 10 faculty members located at American universities that differed in terms of size, focus, and location. Data were collected with four techniques and analyzed using analytic induction and constant comparison. Results : Main findings included the identification of teaching first mentalities, the exploration of two types of educational philosophies (realism and pragmatic idealism), and the uncovering of how and why those philosophies shifted, were enhanced, or remained stagnant. We also identified four types of socialization stories that existed in American higher education that cut across different types of academic institution. Conclusion : This research yields new insights into the nature of faculty socialization and infers that there is still a mountain of knowledge within the secondary organizational socialization stage that has yet to be explored.

title: An Examination of Physical Education Technology Courses in Physical Education Teacher Education
text_snippet: An Examination of Physical Education Technology Courses in Physical Education Teacher Education Purpose : This study explored how physical education-specific technology courses within physical education teacher education (PETE) programs address students’ Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK), given that successful technology integration in PETE remains unclear. Method : A case study design was used to examine six PETE programs’ physical education-specific technology courses within the United States. Semistructured interviews with course instructors and course materials (e.g., syllabi, assignments) were inductively analyzed to explore how they addressed TPACK components and PETE technology standards. Results : All courses addressed varying components of TPACK and PETE technology standards. Additional thematic analysis showed that all courses encouraged (a) hands-on practical experience, (b) technology exploration, (c) empowering teachers, and (d) digital citizenship advocacy. Discussion : PETE programs currently with or those considering a physical education-specific course should ensure they enhance students’ TPACK by specifically addressing technology use in lesson planning, lesson delivery, assessment, and advocacy in program and course experiences.

title: Motivational Climate in Physical Education: How Anxiety and Pleasure Modulate Concentration and Distraction
text_snippet: Motivational Climate in Physical Education: How Anxiety and Pleasure Modulate Concentration and Distraction Purpose : This study examined the relationship between the motivational climate (empowering or disempowering) and pupils’ concentration and distraction in physical education, mediated by basic psychological needs (BPN) satisfaction/frustration, pleasure, and anxiety. Method: In total, 379 French high school pupils ( M age = 15.63; SD age = 0.87) completed a questionnaire regarding the study variables. This study used a structural equation modeling to examine the hypothesized relationships. Results : The motivational climate was found to be related to concentration/distraction. BPN satisfaction/frustration was related to concentration and distraction. This relation was mediated by anxiety and pleasure (empowering climate à BPN satisfaction à pleasure à concentration; disempowering climate à BPN frustration à anxiety à distraction). The model indicates a good fit: comparative-fit index = .93; Tucker–Lewis index = .91; root mean square error of approximation = .071. Discussion/Conclusion : By creating an empowering motivational climate and ensuring that pupils’ competence needs are satisfied or frustrated, teachers can improve pupils’ concentration which is key component of learning.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Systematic Review of Methods of Teaching Swimming to People With Disabilities
text_snippet: Systematic Review of Methods of Teaching Swimming to People With Disabilities This systematic review aimed to analyze the methodologies used to teach swimming skills to individuals with disabilities and followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. 13 studies were reviewed to identify the most effective approaches in aquatic education. The studies analyzed included participants with a range of disabilities, such as autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, and visual impairments. Key findings suggest that tailored methodologies like the Halliwick Method and Water Exercise Swimming Program improve motor and social skills significantly, while inclusive frameworks such as the Sherrill Swimming Model promote participation across diverse groups. In addition, the Comprehensive Aquatic Method offers an innovative framework, which includes cognitive challenges and creative activities promoting social and emotional development. However, gaps remain in addressing sensory disabilities, particularly hearing impairments. This review provides insights for educators and practitioners to develop inclusive aquatic programs while highlighting the need for further research into underexplored populations and socioaffective outcomes.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Received and Perceived Peer Acceptance in Relation to Enjoyment, Social Competence, and Physical Activity in Primary School Physical Education and the Role of Peer-Relatedness Need Satisfaction
text_snippet: Received and Perceived Peer Acceptance in Relation to Enjoyment, Social Competence, and Physical Activity in Primary School Physical Education and the Role of Peer-Relatedness Need Satisfaction Purpose : This study explored associations between actually received and perceived peer acceptance; their role for peer-relatedness need satisfaction; and enjoyment, social competence, and physical activity level during physical education (PE). Method : Two hundred and twenty-seven children (48% boys, mean age: 11.4 years, ± 0.98) from 13 classes of three Dutch primary schools filled in questionnaires to measure their received and perceived peer acceptance, peer-relatedness need satisfaction, enjoyment, and self-perceived social competence in PE. Accelerometers assessed moderate to vigorous physical activity levels during PE. Results : Structural equation models in Mplus showed a medium correlation between received and perceived peer acceptance. Only perceived peer acceptance predicted satisfaction of the peer-relatedness need. Received peer acceptance predicted social competence and moderate to vigorous physical activity, perceived peer acceptance linked to PE enjoyment, and indirectly, via satisfaction of peer relatedness, to social competence. Conclusion : A PE environment where children are, and, feel, socially accepted seems vital for bringing about positive PE experiences.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: The Impact of Team Composition on Student’s Sport Skill Development in Sport Education
text_snippet: The Impact of Team Composition on Student’s Sport Skill Development in Sport Education Purpose : This study explores how diverse team compositions influence table tennis skill development in college students during a Sport Education (SE) season, considering gender and initial skill-level differences. Method : A quasiexperimental design included 64 college students, evenly split into control and experimental groups based on gender. Control group had heterogeneous teams, while experimental group had both heterogeneous and homogeneous teams. The 16-week SE season assessed backhand and forehand blocking skill improvement through two weekly sessions (45 min each). Results : Both groups exhibited skill development, with no significant gender differences. However, the experimental group demonstrated more comparable skill development across different skill levels compared with control group. Conclusion : The study underscores the positive impact of a design combining homogeneous and heterogeneous teams in SE on college students’ table tennis skill development. Educators are advised to consider context-specific factors, including sociocultural influences and sport skill complexity, when structuring team compositions within SE.

journal_name: JOURNAL OF TEACHING IN PHYSICAL EDUCATION
title: Investigating the Influence of Perceived Teaching and Environmental Appraisals on Emotions and Perceived Marginality of Physical Educators
text_snippet: Investigating the Influence of Perceived Teaching and Environmental Appraisals on Emotions and Perceived Marginality of Physical Educators Purpose : As part of a larger project, the purpose of this study was to investigate teacher appraisals about their teaching and environment and its influence on their emotions and perceived marginality. Method : Physical educators ( N = 30; n = 17 females; n = 13 males) participated in an interview grounded in Ecological Dynamics System Theory. Results : Data revealed four themes: (a) students elicit polarizing emotional responses, (b) administrators significantly influence teacher emotion and perceived marginality, (c) advocacy efforts can mitigate anger and anxiety, and (d) high-quality physical education teacher education and discipline specific professional development can enhance positive emotions. Teacher appraisals of their ability and school status influence how they feel and the degree of influence marginality has on them. Discussion/Conclusion : An interconnection exists between teacher emotions and how one may overcome marginality. Suggestions are provided for how appraisals can support future training and professional development.

title: Declining Physical Education Access in U.S. Schools: A State-by-State Analysis of Policy Implementation
text_snippet: Declining Physical Education Access in U.S. Schools: A State-by-State Analysis of Policy Implementation Purpose : This study evaluated student access to physical education in 26 U.S. states, examining weekly minutes, class sizes, and policy implementation practices. Methods : The U.S. Physical Education and Physical Activity Policy questionnaire was distributed to 40,970 physical education teachers across 26 states. Data were collected on weekly minutes, days/week, class sizes, and policy-related practices. Responses were analyzed to assess physical education access and its correlation with class sizes. Results : Findings revealed that student physical education access is below recommendations, with significant between-state variability. Average weekly minutes were 92.8 in elementary, 151.8 in middle school, 185.9 in high school, and 157.8 for students with disabilities. Positive correlations between minutes/week and class sizes suggest that some schools increase class sizes to maintain instructional time. Conclusion : To address declining physical education access, future efforts should focus on engaging educators and policymakers through advocacy, professional development, and best practices in state policies.

title: The Feasibility of Sport Education for Implementation With Third-Grade Students: Proof of Concept
text_snippet: The Feasibility of Sport Education for Implementation With Third-Grade Students: Proof of Concept Purpose : To conduct a “proof of concept” to decide if Sport Education is a viable model for implementation with third-grade students. Method : One hundred and eight students participated in 14-lesson seasons of modified floor hockey that included all six elements outlined by Siedentop in 1994. Seven benchmarks were operationalized to define the success of a Sport Education season and were statistically analyzed, with the outcomes compared to success criteria in percentage terms. Results : Across six of the seven measures, the students comfortably exceeded the success criteria, demonstrating that a well-taught Sport Education season can achieve the goals of the model to help young children to become “players in the fullest sense.” Discussion : Focuses on success criteria effectiveness, feasibility analysis of conditions needed for successful Sport Education implementation, and evaluative potential of proof of concept in other models-based practice.

title: Professionally Developing (or Not): “Learning to Do” Physical Education Teacher Education
text_snippet: Professionally Developing (or Not): “Learning to Do” Physical Education Teacher Education Purpose : This study’s purpose was to explore professional career paths into Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE). More specifically, this study explored critical and/or impactful experiences in learning to do the work of PETE. Method : Participants were 27 professionally active PETE faculty members. Data sources included semistructured interviews, living graphs, and curriculum vitae. Results : Findings describe points in time (when) and impactful events/experiences (how) critical in professionally developing as a teacher educator, including intentionally designed learning experiences, building a support network, teaching experience, coursework and other resources, and trial and error. Discussion/Conclusion : Framed in occupational socialization theory, results are discussed in terms of the inconsistencies of doctoral programs and highlight that emerging PETE faculty did not feel well prepared for teaching roles. Those who felt best prepared to deliver teacher education courses experienced scaffolded, often customized, learning experiences in their doctoral program. Implications for the future of physical education are discussed.

title: Understanding Work-Avoidance Goals for Running in Physical Education
text_snippet: Understanding Work-Avoidance Goals for Running in Physical Education Purpose : To examine mean score changes of students’ work-avoidance (WA) goals for running in physical education from fifth to eighth grade and their relationships with persistence/effort and intention for future running participation. Methods : Participants included 793 American students (427 boys and 366 girls), who were tracked from Grades 5 to 8 in school. Questionnaire data were collected at the end of each school year. Primary data analysis included growth modeling and path analysis. Results : Mean scores of students’ WA goals for running declined from fifth to sixth grade but gradually increased toward the end of eighth grade. Students’ WA goals longitudinally and negatively predicted their persistence/effort and intention for future running participation in physical education. Conclusion : The observed prolonged and negative effects of WA goals on students’ outcomes in the present study suggest a need to develop effective strategies to prevent students from adopting WA goals in physical education settings.

title: Exploring the (Ex/In)clusion of Disability Within Social Justice Physical Education Research
text_snippet: Exploring the (Ex/In)clusion of Disability Within Social Justice Physical Education Research Purpose : The purpose of this study was to explore what trends exist in the identification, description, and inclusion of disability within social justice focused physical education scholarship. Method : Using a documentary analysis approach, this study employed a systematic coding procedure to analyze 140 journal publications from six leading physical education journals using six categories of analysis. Results : Among the 140 analyzed papers, disability was not mentioned in more than half ( n = 71). Among the 69 that did mention disability, many ( n = 32) only used the term in a list as one of several marginalized groups. Among empirical studies, only five included disability as a demographic variable. Four of these papers were focused specifically on disabled people. Discussion/Conclusion : These findings demonstrate a general lack of disability within social justice physical education scholarship, which may be a result of varying perspectives about what social justice scholarship is and who social justice research should be for.

title: Physical Education as a Pathway to Sustainability: Implementing the Personal and Social Responsibility Model to Meet Sustainable Development Goals
text_snippet: Physical Education as a Pathway to Sustainability: Implementing the Personal and Social Responsibility Model to Meet Sustainable Development Goals Reflecting on the urgent need for planetary sustainability and the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals for 2030, this study investigates the critical role of physical education in the educational system toward achieving these objectives. It specifically examines how the Sustainable Development Goals can be integrated with the Personal and Social Responsibility Model to enhance sustainability in education. By presenting a didactic approach and practical examples, like active commuting, and plogging, tailored to suit various levels of Personal and Social Responsibility Model, the study aims to engage students in sustainability efforts. The findings reveal that such activities not only encourage health and well-being but also foster a sense of social and environmental responsibility, promote gender equality, and aim to reduce inequalities among students. Ultimately, incorporating this model into physical education shows considerable promise in instilling important values and responsibilities in students, equipping them to apply these principles in real-world scenarios and positively contributing toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Spanish University Students’ Experiences and Perceptions of the Spectrum of Teaching Styles and Application of the Model Based on the Self-Determination Theory
text_snippet: Spanish University Students’ Experiences and Perceptions of the Spectrum of Teaching Styles and Application of the Model Based on the Self-Determination Theory Purpose : To test the application of the four-group model of teaching styles based on the self-determination theory in a population of Spanish university students and to analyze the Spanish university students’ experiences and perceptions of the teaching styles according to this model. Method : This research followed a descriptive quantitative methodology using a survey. A questionnaire on students’ experiences and perceptions of teaching styles was administered to a total of 667 Spanish university students of physical education (77.8% men and 22.2% women, aged between 18 and 30 years). Results : All the factors presented an acceptable–good reliability index (α ≥ .7), and the multivariate analysis was significant for the variables year and ownership ( p ≤ .05). Conclusion : The four-factor model was applicable to the Spanish university population, and the directive cluster was given higher scores by students in the first year, whereas students in the last year preferred the discovery cluster.

title: Current Practices of Lesson Planning in Physical Education Teacher Education Programs
text_snippet: Current Practices of Lesson Planning in Physical Education Teacher Education Programs Purpose : This study aimed to explore current practices associated with lesson planning in physical education teacher education programs. Method : The study employed a descriptive quantitative research design using survey and lesson plan templates as data sources. A total of 64 physical education teacher education faculty members’ survey responses and 38 lesson plan templates were collected. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze the survey results, and content analyses were employed to examine the lesson plan templates. Results : The majority of the participants responded that they increased the demands on lesson plans as preservice teachers progressed through the program and spent less than 30 min per lesson plan review. The lesson plan templates primarily consisted of three major areas, including lesson overview, tasks and activities, and reflection. Discussion/Conclusion : The practice associated with lesson planning varies at each program. Further investigation into effective practice for lesson planning is essential in future studies.

title: Is an Activity Wristband-Based Intermittent Teaching Unit in the Physical Education Setting Effective for Increasing High School Students’ Weekly Steps? School-Fit Study
text_snippet: Is an Activity Wristband-Based Intermittent Teaching Unit in the Physical Education Setting Effective for Increasing High School Students’ Weekly Steps? School-Fit Study Purpose : To examine the effect of an activity wristband-based intermittent teaching unit (TU) combined with other behavior modification strategies in the physical education setting on high school students’ weekly steps. Method : Seventy-one high school students (49.3% girls) aged 12–16 years performed an 8-week intermittent TU (last 15 min of each session) twice a week. The TU consisted of the following strategies: activity wristband (24 hr), educational counseling, and progressive step goals, among others. Results : The students improved their weekly steps from Week 1 to Weeks 4–8 ( p ≤ .001; d = 0.45–0.58). There was a higher percentage of students who did at least an average of 10,000 steps per day at Week 8 compared with Week 1 ( p = .031; Cramer’s V = 0.246). Conclusion : The studied intermittent TU increased students’ weekly steps and the proportion of students who did at least an average of 10,000 steps per day.

title: Principals’ Perspectives on Quality Physical Education in Australian Primary Schools
text_snippet: Principals’ Perspectives on Quality Physical Education in Australian Primary Schools Purpose : This study examined principals’ perceptions of quality physical education (PE). Principals’ perceptions are important due to their positions in schools and their influence over teacher improvement and student learning. Insights into principal’s perceptions are needed as, in Australia, PE is often marginalized, and afforded less time, and resourcing than “academic” subjects. Methods : Interview data from 14 primary school principals across Kaurna Yerta (Adelaide, South Australia) were thematically analyzed to identify attributes ascribed to quality PE. Results : Principals reported teacher attributes as personal and interpersonal abilities, and pedagogical and content knowledge. School-based attributes relating to resources, specifically facilities and equipment, were also reported. Data pertaining to pedagogy revealed that principals were unfamiliar with the PE curriculum structure, content, and student achievement standards, nor did they recognize unique pedagogical requirements for PE. Conclusion : Responses indicated principals do not necessarily understand or comprehend unique PE-specific pedagogies that enhance PE, nor have deep familiarity with PE.

title: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial to Compare Online and In-Person Motor Skill Acquisition

text_snippet: Student and Teacher Experiences and Perceptions of “Make Basketball Count” – a Program That Delivers Integrated Basketball and Numeracy Lessons for Primary Schools Purpose : Physical activity is beneficial for children’s health and well-being, but competing demands on schools has reduced the amount of time children are active. Integrating physical activity into the school curriculum has shown promise for improving educational outcomes including enjoyment, engagement, and perceived well-being. This study evaluated the feasibility of the Make Basketball Count program, which combined basketball skills with mathematics concepts. Methods : Grade 3 students ( n = 104, aged 9–11 years) from two schools participated in the program, consisting of six weekly physically active math lessons using basketball as a stimulus delivered by qualified teachers and a basketball development officer. Students and teachers completed program evaluation questionnaires. Students also completed semistructured interviews through focus groups. title: Disability Awareness Sport and Physical Education Interventions: A Systematic Literature Review From 1992 to 2023
text_snippet: Disability Awareness Sport and Physical Education Interventions: A Systematic Literature Review From 1992 to 2023 Purpose : The purpose of this review was to examine and describe the characteristics of sport and physical education-focused interventions that have been implemented in educational contexts to raise awareness toward disability. Method : A systematic review of journal-based literature published on disability awareness sport and physical education interventions impacting on students and preservice teachers was conducted. The article selection process included three phases based on PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Results : A total of 43 articles, spanning from 1992 to 2023, were analyzed in this study. Interventions were carried out across primary schools, secondary schools, and university settings, with most research coming from the university setting. title: “I’m Trusting You, Don’t Let Me Down”: One Faculty Member’s Efforts at Employing the Spectrum Model
text_snippet: “I’m Trusting You, Don’t Let Me Down”: One Faculty Member’s Efforts at Employing the Spectrum Model Purpose : The spectrum model is a composite pedagogical model seeking to promote human flourishing. The purpose of this study was to provide a first account of the model in one K–12 school. Freddie, a purposefully recruited faculty member with expertise in models-based practice, was provided the model and instructed to read, interpret, and implement the model with three classes during one semester. Method : Data were collected with eight techniques and analyzed using traditional methods. Results : Findings suggested that Freddie’s organizational structure, method, and content captured the spirit of the model and supported his ability to employ various teaching styles. Factors influencing his reading, interpretation, and implementation of the approach were identified. Conclusion : This study provides a description of flourishing pedagogies and reinforces the argument for developing new pedagogical models in school physical education. Future research dedicated to exploring established and emergent models through the lens of human flourishing is warranted.

title: Exploring Subjective Theories of Assessment Among Preservice Physical Education Teachers in a Master’s Program
text_snippet: Exploring Subjective Theories of Assessment Among Preservice Physical Education Teachers in a Master’s Program Purpose : This study aimed to explore the subjective theories of assessment held by preservice physical education teachers in a master’s program, focusing on each assessment literacy component. Method : Using a descriptive phenomenological approach, 11 master’s program preservice physical education teachers (three females, eight males) were purposefully and conveniently recruited in the study. Data sources were interviews, an online survey, instructor’s notes, and assessment samples. Deductive and inductive thematic analysis in NVivo 12 was employed, ensuring trustworthiness through data triangulation, peer debriefing, and member checking. Results : Four themes were generated across multiple data courses. The themes are (a) understanding of assessment purposes, (b) challenges in assessment implementation, (c) self-referenced assessment interpretation, and (d) critical perspectives on assessment data. Ed.”: Creating Physical Education Learning Environments for 2SLGBTQ+ Preservice Teachers Purpose : Traditionally, physical education (PE) has been a subject that reproduces heteronormativity and hegemonic masculinity. Particularly for Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, or Questioning (2SLGBTQ+) students, PE can be an unsafe and uncomfortable space. Unfortunately, research has also demonstrated that Physical Education Teacher Education programs can perpetuate the same negative and harmful discourse. Individuals who embark on a career in education will spend years in a postsecondary institution learning how to become teachers. Regardless of being in a generalist or a PE specialist degree program, the potential exists for preservice teachers (PSTs) to encounter this subject once again in their postsecondary education. The purpose of this research was to explore how three teacher educators created their PE learning environments for 2SLGBTQ+ PSTs. title: Who Wants To Be a Physical Education Teacher? Identity Development
text_snippet: Who Wants To Be a Physical Education Teacher? Identity Development Purpose : This article delves into analyzing professional identity development among Israeli physical education preservice teachers (PSTs), examining shifts in training programs mandated by the Ministry of Education. Method : One hundred and twenty-three physical education PSTs in three different years answered a validated teacher’s professional identity questionnaire. Two-way analysis of variance was used to detect significant differences between subgroups. Results : Analysis revealed variations among PSTs based on an academic year, with third-year students showing higher levels of commitment and identity. Discussion/Conclusion : The results trace how identity evolves dynamically over 3 years, emphasizing how interactions with stakeholders shape and underscore the importance of these early stages in fostering future professional competence and values, underlining the significance of gradual training. We suggest that teacher educators should acknowledge this dynamic process and consistently support PSTs throughout their training.
